clue.text: It's thrown from ships or aircraft before noon

parts.note: jets are aircraft, the plural matching the word
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the hours before midday

explanation.surface: Something tossed out of a vessel or plane in the morning hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo or gear deliberately cast overboard to lighten a vessel, unlike flotsam which floats off a wreck.

clue.text: One questioned about something dangerous in the river?

indicators.note: the dangerous thing sits inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
a mine is something dangerous, giving A MINE

explanation.surface: Someone being interrogated about a hazard in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a link here, meaning 'concerning'. A MINE sits inside EXE, the Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting a test is put questions by the examiners.

clue.text: Conscious of new test in north-east

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the following words are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A fresh examination given somewhere in the north-east, and someone aware of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it is fodder: the three pieces 'new' rearranges give TESTINNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sentient means having awareness and feeling, so the word is a synonym of aware.

clue.text: Scheme is for volunteers to go up in an aircraft

indicators.note: the turned volunteers are placed inside the aircraft word

parts.note: machine is an old word for an aeroplane

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers join a flight as part of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: MACHINE is an old word for an aeroplane, and the TA is Britain's volunteer reserve army; 'to go up' gives AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or contrive, a verb matching the verb sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Joris, eg, has fresh start as a sea-rover

indicators.note: the first letter is replaced by N, the usual abbreviation for new, read here as fresh

parts.note: Joris is a rider in Browning's poem How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix, so an example of a horseman

explanation.surface: A man named Joris starts out again as a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: Joris galloped in Robert Browning's poem about carrying news from Ghent to Aix. 'has fresh start' swaps the H of HORSEMAN for N (new).
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings who raided by sea from Scandinavia are known as Norsemen.

clue.text: Failing to resist, however

definitions.meaning: not holding out against something, split as two words

explanation.surface: Giving in, nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means not holding out against; as one word it means nevertheless, in spite of that.

clue.text: Observed son after capture by cannibals

parts.note: cannibals in cartoons put their captives in a cooking pot, so the victim is potted

explanation.surface: A boy is seen after being seized by man-eaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' belongs to the second piece: the son, once caught by cannibals, is POTTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted is a synonym of noticed or seen.

clue.text: Indifferent cod — one caught up in lake

indicators.note: the turned fish goes inside the lake word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
one is captured inside the fish

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fish of no great quality is caught and hauled up from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' and 'up' give DIOC, which sits in the lake; 'Indifferent' means middling, not uncaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent can mean neither good nor bad, which is what an ordinary, middling effort is.

clue.text: He thinks nothing is true, for a start

definitions.text: He thinks nothing is true, for a start

parts.note: nihil is Latin for nothing
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word true is used

explanation.surface: A man who believes nothing at all can be true.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: someone who rejects all belief. NIHIL is Latin for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all moral and religious principles, believing that no truth or value exists.

clue.text: Boarding a cart with a Glaswegian, possibly

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon
someone from Glasgow is an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: Getting aboard a wagon alongside a man from Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' looks like climbing aboard but means wooden panelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling lining the lower part of a room's walls, so boarding in the sense of planks.

clue.text: In which one is supported by a trumpeter

definitions.text: In which one is supported by a trumpeter

parts.words: In which one is supported by a trumpeter
parts.note: the trumpeter is not a musician but an elephant, and the rider sits in a seat on its back

explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied seat fixed on an elephant's back, and elephants trumpet.

clue.text: Double share of profit from tropical pods?

indicators.note: the share word appears twice in a row

parts.note: divi is informal British for a dividend, a payout from profits

explanation.surface: Getting twice the dividend from a crop in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVI, British slang for a dividend, appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Divi-divi is a tropical American tree whose curled pods are used in tanning.

clue.text: Way to play a drum or go about acting

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a roll is a rapid continuous drumbeat, and to roll is to play one

explanation.surface: Drumming techniques compared with touring as a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Strolling players were actors who wandered from town to town, so to go about acting is to stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolling players were wandering actors, so the verb can mean to tour while performing.

clue.text: Someone at her dairy looks after the cattle

annotationWithheld.why: Someone at her dairy looks after the cattle (8): the answer runs across someONE AT HER Dairy with no indicator word, and 'Someone' is both fodder and part of the definition (someone who looks after the cattle), so the word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Someone at her dairy looks after the cattle

clue.text: Logical exposition of a clumsy alienator

indicators.note: clumsy suggests the letters of alienator are handled awkwardly into a new order

explanation.surface: A reasoned explanation from someone who drives people away clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoned basis or justification set out for something.

clue.text: Plague in Hungary once

definitions.meaning: A separate city until united with Buda in 1873 to form Budapest

explanation.surface: An epidemic in old Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a nuisance or, archaically, a pestilence; and the half of Budapest east of the Danube was once a city of its own.

clue.text: Wartime pipeline left incomplete by cunning old philosopher

indicators.note: the pipeline's name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: PLUTO (Pipe-Line Under The Ocean) carried fuel under the Channel in the Second World War
arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker sly enough to leave a wartime pipeline unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUTO was the fuel line laid under the English Channel for D-Day; 'left incomplete' drops its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was a Greek biographer and Platonist philosopher of the first century AD.

clue.text: Accepted a quantity of wood

definitions.meaning: a timber measure, the Petrograd ... of 165 cubic feet

explanation.surface: Agreed on an amount of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard practice is accepted practice; and in the timber trade a standard is a fixed volume of sawn wood.

clue.text: Moved to rapture, say, by very little cash

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or carried away

explanation.surface: Thrilled at receiving only a tiny sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, a trifling sum.

clue.text: His products may often be put on a horse

definitions.text: His products may often be put on a horse

parts.words: His products may often be put on a horse
parts.note: the horse is not an animal but a clothes horse, a frame for airing garments

explanation.definitionFit: A clothier makes or sells garments, and a clothes horse is a frame for drying them.

clue.text: Pointers society finds superfluous

parts.note: needles on dials and compasses point

explanation.surface: A society decides some indicators are unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary.

clue.text: Dry description of number of golfer's requisites?

definitions.text: description of number of golfer's requisites?
definitions.meaning: a count of the pegs a golfer uses

explanation.surface: A sober way of counting a golfer's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person drinks no alcohol; split, it reads as the total of a golfer's tees.

clue.text: Scene of dramatic operations in war?

definitions.text: Scene of dramatic operations in war?

parts.words: Scene of dramatic operations in war?
parts.note: both a stage where plays are put on and the region where military operations happen

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is a playhouse, and a theatre of war is an area of military action.

clue.text: Small boat requiring careful handling

definitions.meaning: a vessel that ferries people or supplies to a larger ship

explanation.surface: A dinghy that must be treated gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a small craft attending a larger ship; tender also means delicate or sore.

clue.text: Time to dine on stew?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients, so the letters of to dine on are jumbled

explanation.surface: A suggestion that it is time for a meal of stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the food to be eaten but is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is an old word for midday, a time of day.

clue.text: Rhode Island singer's place of trade

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state
an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: Where a singer from Rhode Island does business.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto was Venice's commercial exchange, and the name came to mean any marketplace.

clue.text: Like the round earth's corners, Donne supposed

definitions.text: Like the round earth's corners, Donne supposed

parts.words: Like the round earth's corners, Donne supposed
parts.note: John Donne's Holy Sonnet opens 'At the round earth's imagin'd corners', and supposed is a synonym of the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Something imagined is conceived in the mind, and a round globe can only have corners in fancy.

clue.text: No spineless type, Stickly-Prickly? Just so

definitions.text: No spineless type, Stickly-Prickly? Just so

parts.words: No spineless type, Stickly-Prickly? Just so
parts.note: a creature covered in spines, named Stickly-Prickly in Kipling's Just So Stories

explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's Just So Stories the spiny animal in the tale of the armadillo is called Stickly-Prickly.

clue.text: For instance, the old thing's going out

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
res is Latin, an old tongue, for thing, with the 's adding S

explanation.surface: An example of an antique object being taken outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like part of the story but defines the answer as a noun: an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out or the act of leaving.
